title: Bradley-Terry Training Can Distort Outcome Probabilities of Initially Accurate Language World Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.25594v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Comparative feedback, in which a judge says which of two candidate outcomes is closer to what happened, is a practical way to train language world models that assign probabilities to an action's outcomes. We show that, fitted with a Bradley-Terry objective, it need not teach the true outcome probabilities and can distort accurate ones. On a simulated robot push with enumerated outcome distributions, this objective takes a model that is accurate on unseen layouts (hazard error 2.4 percentage points, pp) and moves 33 to 43 pp of its probability onto outcomes that none of a condition's enumerated branches produces. The cause is the objective, not the comparisons: its optimum, computed before training, predicts where the model ends up, and a likelihood that knows the judge's rule learns from the same comparisons without the shift. translated_title: Bradley-Terry训练可能扭曲原本准确的语言世界模型的结果概率
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.25594v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：比较反馈（即由评判者指出两个候选结果中哪一个更接近实际发生的情况）是训练为动作结果分配概率的语言世界模型的一种实用方法。我们证明，使用Bradley-Terry目标函数进行拟合时，它未必能教会模型真实的结果概率，甚至可能扭曲原本准确的结果概率。在一个具有枚举结果分布的模拟机器人推动任务中，该目标函数会使一个在未见布局上表现准确的模型（危害误差为2.4个百分点）将33至43个百分点的概率转移到该条件下没有任何枚举分支会产生的结果上。问题的根源在于目标函数本身，而非比较数据：在训练前计算的目标函数最优解可以预测模型最终的去向，而一个了解评判者规则的似然函数能够从相同的比较数据中学习且不产生这种偏移。这种偏移具有鲁棒性：它在未见条件、五种候选法则以及三倍更密集的枚举下均会重现。
tldr: 本文证明Bradley-Terry目标函数在基于比较反馈的训练中无法教会语言世界模型真实的结果概率，反而会将原本准确的模型（危害误差仅2.4个百分点）中33-43个百分点的概率扭曲到实际不可能发生的结果上，且这种失真源于目标函数本身而非比较数据。
en_tdlr: Bradley-Terry training with comparative feedback fails to teach true outcome probabilities and substantially distorts initially accurate language world models, shifting 33-43 percentage points of probability onto impossible outcomes—a distortion caused by the objective itself rather than the comparison data.
